selected_evidence.summary: Both configurations validated; node2 emitted an inventory message and node1 read it from the required file.
Node1's boot ID changed from 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28 to 7b6f2bc7-58a5-47f0-9c98-8b9211648360. The listener, firewall rule, stored data, and fresh log delivery recovered.
Node2's boot ID changed from 03408ac4-bfe4-4151-98bd-1966b0a205af to a01d0f7d-a11d-4835-9fec-ac798341fa05. Rsyslog recovered and a fresh post-restart inventory message reached node1.

commands.command:
cat > /etc/rsyslog.d/30-inventory-forward.conf <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
if ($programname == 'inventory') then {
    action(
        type="omfwd"
        target="10.100.46.10"
        port="514"
        protocol="tcp"
        template="RSYSLOG_SyslogProtocol23Format"
        action.resumeRetryCount="-1"
        queue.type="LinkedList"
        queue.filename="inventory_forward"
        queue.saveOnShutdown="on"
    )
}
ANTRIEB_EOF
restorecon -F /etc/rsyslog.d/30-inventory-forward.conf && rsyslogd -N1 && systemctl restart rsyslog && systemctl is-active rsyslog && systemctl is-enabled rsyslog
